title: Add spatial Locate to universe navigation by reusing the pinned MIT YEIS CameraController center autopilot

scope.subject: Search-result spatial focus inside the native YEIS galaxy view

research_summary: The restored navigator can already open systems directly. The pinned MIT CameraController still includes centerOnDirection(), goToPoint() and autopilot interpolation. A Locate action therefore does not need a new camera animation system. The safest first spatial enhancement is centerOnDirection: keep the visitor in galaxy mode, rotate smoothly toward the resolved YEIS star, preserve the existing galaxy orbit state, and leave Open as the separate action for entering the system. Full goToPoint flight can remain a later scale-transition experiment because it requires additional frame-switch semantics.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT CameraController provides centerOnDirection() using its built-in 0.9-second autopilot quaternion interpolation and goToPoint() for later physical flight.
Pinned MIT UI separates center/focus actions from go-to actions, supporting the product decision to keep Locate and Open distinct.

search_ladder.conclusion: The mother engine already contains the spatial focus behavior and UI semantics.
R3F only needs to pass a focus request into the hosted YEIS scene; it should not own a parallel camera animation.
CameraController.centerOnDirection is the complete subsystem primitive for this locate step.

coverage_matrix.capability: smoothly orient galaxy view toward a search result
coverage_matrix.decision: Use YEIS centerOnDirection rather than animating the R3F camera separately.
The controller remains the single camera authority.
Locate is additive; Enter/Open still enters the system.
Center direction now; defer goToPoint until frame switching and arrival semantics are explicitly validated.

candidates.name: YEIS CameraController.centerOnDirection Locate
candidates.source: pinned MIT CameraController + existing hosted controller instance
candidates.reason: Reuses the camera authority already running the native galaxy view, provides built-in smooth interpolation, and adds no duplicate camera state.

candidates.name: Animate the R3F PerspectiveCamera directly for search focus
candidates.reason: Would create a second camera authority alongside CameraController and risks state drift on the next native input/update.

candidates.name: Keep navigator as direct system-open only
candidates.reason: Stable but misses the exploratory spatial-navigation value already available in the pinned engine.

decision.rationale: Add Locate as a thin request into the existing YEIS CameraController. Keep Open separate and postpone full physical goToPoint flight until system-frame switching is explicitly integrated.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: R3F is the broader framework, but using it directly for locate would bypass the hosted YEIS CameraController that already owns native galaxy orientation and input. That creates duplicate camera authority and worse global state coherence despite broader customization.

decision.fallback: If locate requests arrive before the native galaxy scene is ready, queue the latest request and consume it on the first frame after initialization. Direct Open remains unaffected.
